Bug_Details:
Reference equality used to compare arrays Generally when comparing arrays for equality, the programmer intends to check
that the contents of the arrays are equal rather than that they are actually the
same object. But many commonly used equals methods compare arrays for reference
equality rather than content equality. These include the instance .equals()
method, Guava’s com.google.common.base.Objects#equal(), JDK’s
java.util.Objects#equals(), and Android’s
androidx.core.ObjectsCompat#equals(). If reference equality is needed, == should be used instead for clarity.
Otherwise, use java.util.Arrays#equals() to compare the contents of the
arrays.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the line where 'arr1.equals(arr2)' is used. In Java, 'equals()' method for an array compares the references rather than the contents of the array. To compare the contents of the arrays, 'java.util.Arrays.equals(arr1, arr2)' should be used.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by comparing two integer arrays using the 'equals()' method, which compares references instead of contents. This causes the test case to fail, as the arrays have the same content but are not the same object.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that the bug was not triggered. The test case expected the result of the showBug method to be false, but it was true. Since the arrays arr1 and arr2 are not equal according to reference equality (arr1!= arr2) and the test passed, this suggests that the bug was not present in the showBug method.
